core_idea: Society is not a thing that explains action; it is what has to be explained. Social order is assembled from networks of people and non-humans (technologies, documents, objects), all treated symmetrically as actors. Research follows how actors enrol others, translate interests and make networks hold together or fall apart.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How did a technology, policy, standard or practice come to be established (or fail)?
What role do objects and technologies play alongside people?
Typical data: ethnography, following documents and objects, interviews across many actors, archival tracing.
common_mistakes: Using ANT as a label while still explaining outcomes by 'social factors' decided in advance.
Listing actors without tracing the work of translation and enrolment.
Claiming ANT gives a ready-made method; it is a sensibility for following actors.
